Magnetic flux concentration

Words: 176 Articles: 2
Magnetohydrodynamics OurBigBook.com
Magnetic flux concentration redistributes existing magnetic flux into a smaller area. For a locally straight flux bundle with conserved flux, BA is constant, so decreasing area increases field strength. Converging convection, field-line stretching and flux expulsion can produce concentrations; finite magnetic diffusivity opposes them and Lorentz force feedback limits the kinematic approximation. Redistribution alone is not evidence of net dynamo action.

Equipartition magnetic field (Beq​=μ0​ρ​U)

Words: 49
Magnetic flux concentration OurBigBook.com
Equating magnetic energy density B2/(2μ0​) to kinetic energy density ρU2/2 defines this order-of-magnitude field. It marks when a weak-field kinematic treatment of a given flow can fail, not a universal upper bound on concentrated fields. Gas-pressure confinement, compression, partial evacuation and dynamic pressure can allow stronger local fields.

Convective collapse

Words: 74
Magnetic flux concentration OurBigBook.com
A compressible intensification mechanism for a thin, nearly vertical flux tube in a superadiabatic atmosphere. An unstable downflow drains material and lowers internal gas pressure; approximate lateral balance pi​+B2/(2μ0​)=pe​ then permits the tube to contract and its field to strengthen at nearly conserved magnetic flux. It relies on compressibility and thermal evolution, which are absent from a strict Boussinesq approximation. Dynamic photospheric structures need not satisfy thin-tube equilibrium, so this mechanism does not explain every intense field concentration.

Magnetostrophic balance (2ρΩz^×u=−∇p+fb​+J×B)

Words: 373 Articles: 4
Magnetohydrodynamics OurBigBook.com
The leading force balance in a rapidly rotating conducting fluid when inertial and viscous forces are small, while Coriolis force, pressure, buoyancy and Lorentz force density remain significant. The Rossby number and Ekman number measure the omitted inertia and bulk viscosity. Rotation does not balance an arbitrary magnetic torque: impenetrable axisymmetric boundaries impose the Taylor constraint. Magnetic diffusion can remain in the induction equation even when viscosity is neglected in momentum balance.

Taylor constraint (∫Cs​​(J×B)ϕ​dϕdz=0)

Words: 311 Articles: 3
Magnetostrophic balance OurBigBook.com
In inviscid magnetostrophic balance within an impenetrable axisymmetric container, with no azimuthal buoyancy or external mechanical torque, the cylindrically integrated Lorentz force density must vanish on every cylinder coaxial with rotation. The azimuthal pressure derivative integrates to zero, and the cylindrical Coriolis integral is proportional to net radial flux, zero by incompressibility and impermeability. Multiplying by cylinder area and lever arm gives the equivalent zero-torque form. This rotating-fluid condition is distinct from magnetic-helicity relaxation to a force-free plasma state. Its original primary source is Taylor's 1963 rotating-fluid paper.

Viscous regularization of the Taylor constraint (TL​(s)+Tν​(s)=0)

Words: 88
Taylor constraint OurBigBook.com
With small viscosity, the azimuthal cylindrical balance permits Lorentz force torque to be cancelled by viscous stress. For ordinary no-slip rotating boundaries an Ekman layer gives stress of order ρΩLUE​, larger than the order-E bulk viscous correction at fixed velocity. Thus bounded small-E flows approach a magnetostrophic Taylor state but need not satisfy its constraint exactly at finite viscosity. An order-one uncompensated magnetic torque would require a divergent flow as E→0, invalidating the assumed small-inertia balance. Stress-free boundaries remove the leading no-slip friction and require their own torque/regularity conditions.

Geostrophic flow preserving the Taylor constraint (DTB​[∇×(u×B)+η∇2B]=0)

Words: 95
Taylor constraint OurBigBook.com
For an instantaneous magnetostrophic Taylor state, the momentum equation leaves a geostrophic null component ug​=sω(s)ϕ^​. Decompose the velocity into this component and a particular ageostrophic flow, substitute the induction equation into the displayed derivative constraint, and solve the resulting linear equation for ω with magnetic boundary conditions imposed. When magnetic surface torque vanishes, the geostrophic part is μ0−1​∂s​[s3∫Cs​​Bs2​dϕdzω′]. Boundary terms generally cannot be discarded for an insulating exterior; the primary analysis is Hardy and collaborators' boundary-compatible geostrophic-flow construction. Regularity and an angular-momentum normalization fix remaining homogeneous freedoms when the magnetic coupling is nondegenerate.

Magnetostrophic Taylor state

Words: 44
Taylor constraint OurBigBook.com
A divergence-free magnetic field satisfying the Taylor constraint on all geostrophic cylinders. It is a compatibility condition for slow rotating-fluid balance, not a local force-free condition. To retain such a state as magnetic induction proceeds, the velocity must also preserve the time derivative of the cylindrical torque constraint.

Mean-field electrodynamics (E=⟨u×b⟩)

Words: 59
Magnetohydrodynamics OurBigBook.com
Mean-field electrodynamics applies averaging and a response closure to magnetic induction in a fluctuating conducting fluid. The mean equation contains the correlated mean-field electromotive force in the title. Scale separation permits a local expansion into alpha transport, turbulent diffusion and higher gradients; general anisotropic or finite-memory statistics require tensorial and nonlocal responses. A mean-field dynamo is a self-exciting application of this framework, not a consequence of averaging alone.

Kinematic magnetic dynamo (Dt​B=(B⋅∇)u)

Words: 217 Articles: 4
Magnetohydrodynamics OurBigBook.com
A kinematic magnetic dynamo studies magnetic field amplification by a prescribed fluid flow, neglecting the field's feedback on the velocity through the Lorentz force. With incompressibility and zero magnetic diffusivity, a Lagrangian field vector evolves by its local velocity-gradient matrix. A growth law derived in this approximation cannot hold indefinitely once magnetic stresses significantly change the flow.

Gaussian white-noise magnetic stretching (B˙i​=σim​Bm​)

Words: 168 Articles: 3
Kinematic magnetic dynamo OurBigBook.com
For a trace-free isotropic Gaussian white noise velocity gradient with covariance ⟨σim​(t)σjn​(t′)⟩=κ2​δ(t−t′)[δij​δmn​−(δim​δjn​+δin​δjm​)/4], interpret the multiplicative equation as the Stratonovich integral limit of smooth velocity fluctuations. The causal Furutsu–Novikov formula has endpoint weight one half. It gives Pt​=(κ2​/2)∂i​[(B2δij​−Bi​Bj​/2)∂j​P] for the vector probability density function.

Lognormal magnetic-field amplification (ln(B/B0​)∼N(3Dt,2Dt))

Words: 42
Gaussian white-noise magnetic stretching OurBigBook.com
Set x=ln(B/B0​) and f=BF in the radial magnetic-field Fokker-Planck equation. Then ft​=Dfxx​−3Dfx​, so f is a Gaussian distribution drifting at speed 3D. For initial magnitude B0​>0, F=[B4πDt​]−1exp[−(ln(B/B0​)−3Dt)2/(4Dt)]. This lognormal distribution has moments B0q​eDq(q+3)t; the width of its logarithm grows as 2Dt​.

Magnetic stretching moment growth (∂t​⟨Bq⟩=Dq(q+3)⟨Bq⟩)

Words: 36
Gaussian white-noise magnetic stretching OurBigBook.com
Twice integrating the radial magnetic-field Fokker-Planck equation by parts gives the displayed law when moments and endpoint terms are controlled. In particular ⟨B2⟩ grows at rate 10D=2γ, with γ=5κ2​/4. The corresponding magnetic energy density is ⟨B2⟩/(8π) in Gaussian units.

Radial magnetic-field Fokker-Planck equation (Ft​=D∂B​(B2FB​−2BF),D=κ2​/4)

Words: 55
Gaussian white-noise magnetic stretching OurBigBook.com
For an isotropic initial ensemble in Gaussian white-noise magnetic stretching, F(B)=4πB2P(B) is the magnitude probability density function. The radial vector equation Pt​=D(B2PBB​+4BPB​) gives the displayed conservative Fokker-Planck equation. Its integral is conserved under zero endpoint probability flux. For an anisotropic initial vector distribution, use the angularly averaged magnitude density instead; isotropic noise alone does not make arbitrary initial data isotropic.

Theta pinch (B=B(r)z^)

Words: 93 Articles: 1
Magnetohydrodynamics OurBigBook.com
A theta pinch is a cylindrical plasma configuration with axial magnetic field and azimuthal electric current. For a static equilibrium without gravity, the radial Lorentz force gives d[p+B2/(8π)]/dr=0 in Gaussian units. This straight-field configuration has no field-line curvature drive of the usual interchange instability.

Positive ideal energy of a theta pinch (δW≥0)

Words: 57
Theta pinch OurBigBook.com
For an admissible Fourier fluid Lagrangian displacement ξ(r)eimθ+ikz, put D⊥​=(rξr​)′/r+imξθ​/r and D=D⊥​+ikξz​. Force balance cancels every magnetic-field-gradient cross term in the magnetohydrodynamic energy principle, leaving an integrand γp∣D∣2+B2[∣D⊥​∣2+k2(∣ξr​∣2+∣ξθ​∣2)]/(4π). For p≥0, γ>0, this is nonnegative. Neutral displacements can exist, so stability here means absence of negative-energy exponentially growing ideal modes, not strictly positive energy for every displacement.

Hall magnetohydrodynamics (Hall MHD)

Words: 211 Articles: 2
Magnetohydrodynamics OurBigBook.com
Hall magnetohydrodynamics retains bulk ion inertia but freezes magnetic flux into the electron velocity ue​=u−j/(en). With constant density, negligible electrical resistivity and electron inertia, Gaussian units give j=c∇×B/(4π) and ∂t​B=∇×[(u−c∇×B/(4πen))×B]. The ion velocity still satisfies the magnetohydrodynamic momentum equation. Neglecting that velocity gives electron magnetohydrodynamics, a further approximation rather than a synonym for the complete Hall system.

Fast-time electron-MHD limit of Hall magnetohydrodynamics (l≪di​,τ≪l/vA​)

Words: 84
Hall magnetohydrodynamics OurBigBook.com

For an imposed field B0​ in a layer of depth d, the Chandrasekhar number compares magnetic tension with viscous and magnetic-diffusive effects. In thermal-time magnetoconvection equations, the linear magnetic-force coefficient is σQκ​=σζQCh​. Specifying the convention prevents a missing diffusivity factor in a dispersion relation.

Magnetic buoyancy instability

Words: 441 Articles: 6
Magnetohydrodynamics OurBigBook.com
A magnetic buoyancy instability is a gravitational instability of a magnetized stratified fluid in which displacements of the gas and magnetic field can release Newtonian gravitational potential energy. Magnetic pressure supports part of the weight. Both interchange displacements and undular displacements can enter this broad category; Parker instability is the undular mechanism involving drainage along bent magnetic field lines.

Isothermal interchange criterion for magnetic buoyancy (Bd(B/ρ)/dz<0)

Words: 69
Magnetic buoyancy instability OurBigBook.com
A horizontal flux tube displaced without bending preserves B/ρ by magnetic flux freezing. If thermal exchange keeps its temperature equal to its new surroundings, lateral magnetic pressure balance gives (cT2​+vA2​)(ρi′​−ρ′)=ρB(B/ρ)′/μ0​. Here cT2​=p/ρ, vA2​=B2/(μ0​ρ), and primes denote the response to a small vertical displacement from an equilibrium. Its linear buoyancy acceleration is −gB(B/ρ)′ξ/[μ0​(cT2​+vA2​)]. Thus local interchange is unstable when B(B/ρ)′<0, equivalently (B2/ρ2)′<0. This fast-thermal-exchange criterion differs from the adiabatic localized interchange criterion for a magnetized atmosphere.

Localized interchange criterion for a magnetized atmosphere (−dzdlnρ​<γp+B2/μ0​ρg​)

Words: 58
Magnetic buoyancy instability OurBigBook.com
For disturbances constant along the horizontal magnetic field, the minimized energy density is ρg[−(lnρ)′−ρg/(γp+C)]∣ξz​∣2. If its coefficient is nonnegative everywhere, the full energy is nonnegative. If it is strictly negative at a point of a smooth equilibrium, a compactly supported vertical displacement in a neighbouring interval gives negative energy. These interchange motions compress gas and magnetic pressure together.

Parker instability

Words: 269 Articles: 3
Magnetic buoyancy instability OurBigBook.com
Parker instability is an undular magnetic buoyancy instability of a gravitationally stratified atmosphere supported partly by magnetic pressure. A bent horizontal magnetic field can permit gas to drain along its magnetic field lines, leaving buoyant rising regions. Magnetic tension resists bending, so wavelengths and boundary conditions affect the instability threshold. For a magnetized isothermal atmosphere, the unrestricted-wavevector threshold is given by the magnetic buoyancy energy criterion.

Choosing the square to vanish and then taking a sufficiently small nonzero ky​ gives negative energy exactly when the displayed strict criterion holds somewhere. A fixed prescribed wavenumber retains the stabilizing Cky2​ tension term; the criterion asserts existence of an allowed nonzero wavenumber. The associated along-field displacement lets material drain while magnetic flux bends.

Two uniform horizontal magnetic fields on either side of a horizontal interface exert no bulk force, but their magnetic pressures differ. A stronger field below means denser gas above, supplying a Rayleigh-Taylor instability even though each half-space is hydrostatic.

Their comparison gives the magnetic diffusion time, not merely the rotation period. It diverges as conductivity becomes infinite. Combining its curvature force with conservation of angular momentum gives the restoring coefficient D above. A local incompressible radial-vertical mode has ω2=(kz2​/k2)D. This is distinct from weak-field magnetorotational instability: a steeply increasing toroidal field can release current energy even without differential rotation.

For Bϕ​∝rp, constant density and Keplerian κ2=Ω2, the Michael criterion for axisymmetric toroidal-field interchange becomes Ω2−2(p−1)vA2​/r2. Instability therefore requires p>1 and vA2​>r2Ω2/[2(p−1)]. For a field varying on the radial scale r, this is an orbital-speed field, much stronger than a gas-pressure-scale field with vA​≲cs​∼HΩ in a thin disk. Steep radial field gradients require the exact derivative criterion rather than this scale estimate. The instability is powered by the toroidal field distribution and is distinct from weak vertical-field magnetorotational instability.
